deciding_assertions: expect-timeout.spec.ts 'should fail like a timeout when the signal is aborted mid-assertion' and 'should fail the assertion when the signal is already aborted': expect(...).toBeVisible/toHaveURL({signal}) must fail with error.name not 'AbortError' and the exact text 'Error: The assertion was aborted: stop it' / '... already aborted' in the matcher message; page-filechooser.spec.ts 'should abort with signal': waitForEvent rejection must have name 'AbortError' and cause equal to the raw abort reason.
reason: The issue asks for a signal option on waitFor* APIs and gives no error shape. The tests instead check signal on expect() assertions (not waitFor* APIs) with a new exact message 'The assertion was aborted: <reason>', and change waitForEvent's abort error to an AbortError with cause; the packet shows the base waiter already accepted signal and rejected on abort (old test passed with the reason as message). A narrowest reasonable fix that adds signal to waitFor* APIs and rejects with the abort reason fails all three fail-to-pass tests.

deciding_assertions: test-locks.spec.ts: every test declares test('x', { lock: 'shared' | [...] }, body) and test.describe('s', { lock: 'shared' }, ...); 'should validate lock in test details' expects output to contain 'details.lock'; 'should hold the lock for the whole file group in default mode' expects a lock on one test to cover the whole file.
reason: The issue proposes an option named 'locks' (a list) on the test; the tests use a singular 'lock' detail that accepts a string or array, so a fix that implements 'locks' as the issue asks fails all fail-to-pass tests. The tests also require describe-level locks, a 'details.lock' validation message, and file-group lock scope in default mode, none of which the issue states.

deciding_assertions: reporter.spec.ts '--add-reporter should append to configured reporters instead of replacing them': runs with additionalArgs ['--add-reporter=./added-reporter.js'] and expects output from both reporters.
reason: The issue asks for a CLI flag named '--append-reporter'. The test passes '--add-reporter', a name the issue never gives. A fix that adds '--append-reporter' exactly as requested fails the test (unknown option).

deciding_assertions: playwright.trace.spec.ts 'should record test annotations in trace': parseTrace(...).model.annotations toEqual [{note1, static}, {note2, dynamic}, {type: 'note3'}].
reason: The issue asks to show test annotations in the trace viewer Metadata tab. The test reads a new internal TraceModel property named 'annotations' holding a flat array of {type, description}. A reasonable fix that writes annotations into the trace and shows them in the Metadata tab, but exposes them under another model property or reads them in the UI from the context entry, fails this assertion; 'annotations' follows the testTimeout precedent, so many fixes would pass, hence medium.

deciding_assertions: browsercontext-storage-state.spec.ts 'should round-trip OPFS': storageState({opfs: true}).origins toEqual [{origin, localStorage: [], opfs: [{path: 'hello.txt', type: 'file', base64}, {path: 'nested', type: 'directory'}, {path: 'nested/data.bin', ...}, {path: 'nested/empty', type: 'directory'}]}]; global-fetch-cookie.spec.ts 'should preserve origin storage on import/export of storage state' feeds and expects the same flat {path, type, base64} entries.
reason: The issue gives the option name 'opfs' (with alternatives) and says file contents can be base64, but gives no serialization schema. The tests require one exact shape: a flat list sorted by name with '/'-joined paths, fields 'path', 'type' ('file' | 'directory') and 'base64', directories listed before their children. A reasonable fix that serializes a nested tree, or uses other field names, fails both fail-to-pass tests.

deciding_assertions: mcp/recorder.spec.ts: MCP tools 'browser_start_recording' / 'browser_stop_recording' with messages 'Recording started', 'Recording stopped. Recorded actions:' plus a ```js block, 'No actions were recorded.', 'Recording is already in progress', 'No recording in progress'; cli-devtools.spec.ts 'recording-start-stop': CLI commands 'recording-start' / 'recording-stop'; recorder-api.spec.ts 'should not amend the last action with a signal from another page': dialog signal code is ''.
reason: The issue only asks 'could we support codegen in MCP' or, as an alternative, attaching codegen to the browser extension. The tests need new tool and CLI command names, exact output and error texts, and a recorder signal fix for another page, none of which the issue gives. Any fix that picks other names, other messages, or the extension option fails the tests.

deciding_assertions: browsercontext-har.spec.ts interceptAPIRequests > should fulfill APIRequestContext requests from HAR: replayed.timing() toEqual all nine fields -1, startTime included; browsercontext-fetch.spec.ts should return timing / for https: domainLookupStart toBe 0, connectStart toBe domainLookupEnd, requestStart toBe connectEnd
reason: The issue asks for APIResponse.timing() with the shape of Request.timing() over the timings that fetch.ts already records; the narrowest fix maps those timings and passes the two fetch tests. The issue never mentions responses served from a HAR file, and the test needs all values -1 there, startTime included. A fix that leaves timing absent there, uses Request's defaults (startTime is not documented as -1), or fills a start time fails that assertion.

deciding_assertions: reporter-base.spec.ts should omit tags when omitTags is set / from failures when omitTags is set: reporter ['list', { omitTags: true }]; should omit tags via the PLAYWRIGHT_LIST_OMIT_TAGS environment variable
reason: The issue proposes an appendTags option (default true) for the list and line reporters. The tests pass a different option name, omitTags, and an environment variable PLAYWRIGHT_LIST_OMIT_TAGS that the issue never gives. The fix that the issue proposes (appendTags: false) fails all three fail-to-pass tests.

deciding_assertions: cli-core.spec.ts upload multiple files: cli('upload', front, back) as positionals; cli-parsing.spec.ts missing variadic argument: error contains "'files' argument: expected string, received undefined"; cli-help.spec.ts prints variadic command help: 'playwright-cli upload <files...>'
reason: The issue offers two shapes, a variadic positional or a repeatable --path like drop. The tests need the variadic one, so a --path fix fails the upload test. The issue also says that the variadic shape it verified reports "'files' argument: Invalid input" for a bare upload, and it does not ask to change that. The test needs the 'expected string, received undefined' message, so the variadic fix as the issue describes it fails that test.

deciding_assertions: har.spec.ts should close the context when saving the har fails: recordHar path under a regular file; context.close() rejects with /ENOTDIR|ENOENT|EEXIST/, the 'close' event fires, a second close() resolves
reason: The issue reports that context.close() hangs with recordHar on valid paths in CI. It gives no cause and never mentions a failed HAR write. The test covers only the case where the HAR save fails, and it needs close() to reject with the file system error. A fix that makes close finish by logging or ignoring the error fails rejects.toThrow, and a fix aimed at another cause of the hang does not touch this path.

deciding_assertions: screencast.spec.ts start size is ignored while tracing is active: video frames 800x600 although size 1000x750 was asked; screencast.spec.ts tracing screenshots size sets the shared capture size and tracing.spec.ts should produce screencast frames of the requested size / should respect screencast quality: context.tracing.start({ screencast: { size } }) and { screencast: { quality } }
reason: The issue expects page.screencast.start({ size }) to fill the requested frame, whether or not tracing is on, as with trace off and recordVideo. The test expects the size to be ignored, which gives an 800x600 video. The other tests pass a new tracing.start option, screencast: { size, quality }, that the issue never names (it says the trace size is not configurable). A fix that captures at the larger requested size fails the first test, and no fix from the issue alone passes the other three.

deciding_assertions: mcp/recorder.spec.ts clients sharing a context only receive their own recordings: client2 start is accepted and both transcripts kept separate; recorder-api.spec.ts and selector/locator generator specs: context._showRecorder, _startRecording, _stopRecording; messages 'Recorder is shown, close it before starting a recording.' and 'Recording is in progress, stop it before showing the recorder.'
reason: The issue offers two fixes: refuse the second start, or keep the recordings separate. The MCP test needs the separate recordings, so the refuse fix fails it. Most fail-to-pass tests call the renamed internal methods _showRecorder, _startRecording and _stopRecording in place of _enableRecorder and _disableRecorder, and two new error texts that the issue never gives, so any fix that keeps the existing names fails about 90 tests.

deciding_assertions: expect-timeout.spec.ts 'aborted mid-assertion' and 'already aborted': expect(locator).toBeVisible / expect(page).toHaveURL with { signal } must fail with the exact text 'Error: The assertion was aborted: stop it' and error.name not 'AbortError'; page-filechooser.spec.ts 'should abort with signal': waitForEvent rejection must have name 'AbortError' and cause equal to the abort reason
reason: The issue asks for a signal option on waitFor* APIs; the waiter already handled signal before the fix (the existing waitForEvent signal test passed), so the stated case works. The tests instead need signal support in expect matchers, which the issue does not name, an exact new message 'The assertion was aborted: ...', and a rejection of class AbortError with the reason in cause. A narrowest reasonable fix that adds or keeps signal on waitFor* APIs and rejects with the reason fails all three fail-to-pass tests.

deciding_assertions: test-locks.spec.ts: every fail-to-pass test declares test('...', { lock: 'shared' } or { lock: ['lock-a','lock-b'] }, ...); 'should support locks declared on a describe group' uses test.describe(..., { lock }); 'should validate lock in test details' expects output to contain 'details.lock'; 'should hold the lock for the whole file group in default mode' expects a lock on a1 to also cover a2
reason: The issue proposes a 'locks' list option, passed as an option of test(). The tests pass a 'lock' key (string or array) in test details, so a fix that implements the issue's 'locks' option fails every fail-to-pass test. The describe-level lock, the 'details.lock' error text and the rule that a lock covers the whole file group are also not in the issue.

deciding_assertions: reporter.spec.ts '--add-reporter should append to configured reporters instead of replacing them': runs with additionalArgs ['--add-reporter=./added-reporter.js'] and expects output from both reporters
reason: The issue asks for a CLI option named --append-reporter. The test passes --add-reporter, a flag that the real fix adds and the issue never gives. A fix that adds --append-reporter as asked makes the CLI reject the unknown flag and fails the test.

deciding_assertions: playwright.trace.spec.ts 'should record test annotations in trace': parseTrace(...).model.annotations toEqual [{note1, static}, {note2, dynamic}, {type: note3}]
reason: The issue asks to show static and runtime annotations in the trace viewer Metadata tab, but gives no storage location or property name. The test reads a new TraceModel property 'annotations'. A reasonable fix that records the annotations in the trace and shows them in the Metadata tab through another field or event (for example a separate trace event read by the metadata view, or a field named testAnnotations) fails this assertion. The name follows the sibling testTimeout pattern, so a reader could call it a natural choice.

deciding_assertions: browsercontext-storage-state.spec.ts 'should round-trip OPFS': storageState({ opfs: true }).origins toEqual [{ origin, localStorage: [], opfs: [{ path: 'hello.txt', type: 'file', base64 }, { path: 'nested', type: 'directory' }, { path: 'nested/data.bin', ... }, { path: 'nested/empty', type: 'directory' }] }]; global-fetch-cookie.spec.ts 'should preserve origin storage on import/export of storage state': the same flat opfs entry format round-trips through request.storageState({ indexedDB: true, opfs: true })
reason: The issue gives the option name 'opfs' and says to use base64 for file contents. It does not give the serialized format. The tests assert one exact format: a flat, sorted list with keys path (slash-joined relative path), type 'file' or 'directory', and base64. A reasonable fix that serializes OPFS as a nested tree, or with other key names or order, captures and restores OPFS correctly but fails both toEqual assertions.

deciding_assertions: mcp/recorder.spec.ts: MCP tools 'browser_start_recording' and 'browser_stop_recording' with texts 'Recording started', 'Recording stopped. Recorded actions:' plus a fenced code block, 'No actions were recorded.', 'Recording is already in progress', 'No recording in progress', and python output with --codegen=python; cli-devtools.spec.ts 'recording-start-stop': CLI commands recording-start and recording-stop; recorder-api.spec.ts 'should not amend the last action with a signal from another page': a dialog signal on page2 has empty code
reason: The issue is a vague request that offers two options: codegen in MCP, or attaching the existing codegen command to the browser extension. It gives no tool names, commands or messages. The tests need new MCP tool names, new CLI command names and exact response texts, plus a recorder signal fix that the issue does not mention. Any fix that chooses other names, the extension option, or other wording fails the fail-to-pass tests.

deciding_assertions: browsercontext-har.spec.ts interceptAPIRequests > should fulfill APIRequestContext requests from HAR: replayed.timing() toEqual an object with every field -1, including startTime: -1. (browsercontext-fetch.spec.ts should return timing / for https: domainLookupStart 0, connectStart == domainLookupEnd, requestStart == connectEnd, secureConnectionStart -1 on http.)
reason: The issue asks for APIResponse.timing() with the shape of Request.timing() for network requests and never mentions responses served from a HAR file. The narrowest reasonable fix fills timing on the network path and gives some fallback elsewhere; a fallback with startTime as the request wall time or 0 (the Request default), or no timing object, fails the HAR test, which needs startTime -1, a value the documented meaning of startTime does not give. The two fetch tests follow from mapping the already recorded socket events and pass with that fix.

deciding_assertions: reporter-base.spec.ts should omit tags when omitTags is set / from failures when omitTags is set: reporter ['list', { omitTags: true }]; should omit tags via the PLAYWRIGHT_LIST_OMIT_TAGS environment variable: env PLAYWRIGHT_LIST_OMIT_TAGS=1 hides appended tags.
reason: The issue proposes one option, appendTags (default true), used as ['list', { appendTags: false }]. The tests pass a different option name, omitTags, and a new environment variable PLAYWRIGHT_LIST_OMIT_TAGS that the issue does not give. A fix that adds appendTags exactly as the issue proposes fails all fail-to-pass tests.

deciding_assertions: cli-core.spec.ts upload multiple files: cli('upload', front, back) as positionals; cli-help.spec.ts prints variadic command help: 'playwright-cli upload <files...>'; cli-parsing.spec.ts missing variadic argument: bare upload gives "error: 'files' argument: expected string, received undefined".
reason: The issue offers two shapes (variadic positional or repeatable --path); the tests need the variadic positional and its help text, so a --path fix fails. The issue also states that its preferred variadic fix, as verified, makes bare upload report "'files' argument: Invalid input"; the test needs the old "expected string, received undefined" text, so the fix exactly as the issue proposes it fails the missing-argument test unless it also changes the union error formatting.

deciding_assertions: har.spec.ts should close the context when saving the har fails: recordHar path under a regular file; context.close() rejects with /ENOTDIR|ENOENT|EEXIST/, the 'close' event fires, and a second context.close() resolves.
reason: The issue reports a teardown hang with recordHar in CI but gives no trigger and never mentions a failed HAR write. The test checks only the save-failure path (close must reject with the fs error yet still close the context, and a repeat close must resolve); a fix aimed at another plausible hang cause in HAR recording or close does not cover it. The rejection itself follows existing code that throws the save error, so the deciding gap is the unstated trigger.

deciding_assertions: screencast.spec.ts start size is ignored while tracing is active: screencast size 1000x750 with tracing on gives a video of 800x600; tracing screenshots size sets the shared capture size: context.tracing.start({ screencast: { size } }); tracing.spec.ts should produce screencast frames of the requested size / should respect screencast quality: tracing.start({ screencast: { size } }) and ({ screencast: { quality } }).
reason: The issue expects page.screencast.start({ size }) to fill the requested frame size regardless of tracing. The test asserts the opposite: the requested size is ignored and the video is 800x600. The other tests need a new screencast option of tracing.start with size and quality, which the issue does not give (it says the trace size is not configurable). A fix that scales the capture to the requested size fails all four.

deciding_assertions: recorder-api.spec.ts and inspectorTest/locator-generator/selector-generator: calls context._showRecorder, _startRecording, _stopRecording (renamed internal API); errors 'Recorder is shown, close it before starting a recording.' and 'Recording is in progress, stop it before showing the recorder.'; mcp recorder.spec.ts clients sharing a context only receive their own recordings: client2 start succeeds and its transcript contains client1's Beta click.
reason: The issue offers two designs (refuse the second start or keep recordings separate); the MCP test needs the second and even expects client1's Beta click in client2's transcript, which the issue says should not happen. Most fail-to-pass tests fail only because they call new internal method names (_showRecorder, _startRecording, _stopRecording) and assert new error texts that the issue does not give. A fix that refuses the second start, or that keeps per-client sinks under the old names, fails these tests.

deciding_assertions: All fail-to-pass tests pass a new option `noCertificate: true` in clientCertificates; validate input expects 'noCertificate is set together with cert, key, passphrase or pfx'; 'should throw when noCertificate and a real certificate are both set' expects 'clientCertificates for origin "..." mix noCertificate with a real certificate'; pass-to-pass 'should not intercept TLS for origins without a client certificate' must keep passing.
reason: The issue calls this a regression and asks to restore the documented behaviour (a certificate for a non-matching origin makes the proxy reject client certificates for all other origins). The narrowest reasonable fix restores that interception; it does not know the new option name `noCertificate` or the two new error texts, and it breaks the existing pass-to-pass test that keeps origins without a certificate un-intercepted.

deciding_assertions: golden/to-have-screenshot/aria tests: `update-snapshots=missing` writes missing snapshots and exits 0 with the test passed; new value `update-snapshots=default` keeps the old failing behaviour; config.spec 'should work with undefined values and base' expects testInfo.config.updateSnapshots to be 'default'.
reason: The issue asks for a new value `--update-snapshots=missing-no-failure` and keeps `missing` as it is. The narrowest reasonable fix adds that value; it fails every test that expects the existing `missing` mode to stop failing, and the tests that use a new `default` mode and expect it as the config default.

deciding_assertions: cli-emulation 'set and clear media features': playwright-cli commands set-color-scheme/clear-color-scheme, set-reduced-motion, set-forced-colors, set-contrast, set-media and their clear-* forms; cli-help 'prints emulation help after storage': an 'Emulation:' help section right after 'Storage:'; emulation.spec 'browser_emulate_media requires a media feature': empty call is an error containing 'Specify at least one media feature to emulate.'; exact code strings including null values.
reason: The issue proposes an MCP tool `browser_emulate_media` with all parameters optional plus a `--color-scheme` launch flag. A fix that does exactly that fails the tests for the new playwright-cli commands and help section that the issue never names, and fails the empty-call test, which expects an error with an exact new message where the issue says omitted features stay unchanged.

deciding_assertions: All tests use reporter name 'failures', a new CLI flag '--reporter-only-failures', and a per-reporter option `onlyFailures` (json, junit, html filtering, blob kept complete, merge-reports, --list not filtered, quiet, slow-test report, live retry output).
reason: The issue offers several designs (`--reporter=only-failures`, or a `quiet`/`failuresOnly` option on `list`) and gives none of the names the tests use. A fix that adds an `only-failures` reporter as in the issue example fails every test, which also cover filtering of json, junit and html reports and blob merging that the issue does not ask for.

deciding_assertions: locator-any-frame 'should treat elements inside hidden iframe as hidden' and locator-frame 'should wait for hidden iframe to become visible': `button.click({ timeout: 1000 })` error message contains 'element is inside a hidden frame, retrying'; also the cross-origin iframe case.
reason: The issue asks that visibility checks (toBeHidden, and by extension isVisible/toBeVisible/waitFor) treat elements inside a `visibility: hidden` iframe as hidden, which a reasonable fix does. The tests also require the click actionability log to contain a new exact text 'element is inside a hidden frame, retrying', which the issue never mentions; a fix that only corrects the visibility checks, or logs another text, fails those two tests.

deciding_assertions: 'should reject invalid signCount': credentials.create with signCount -1 must throw with 'signCount must be between 0 and 4294967295, got -1' and store no credential.
reason: The issue asks only to accept `signCount` in credentials.create and return it from credentials.get; the seed-and-report and storageState tests follow from that because the counter already increments. The narrowest reasonable fix passes the value through without range checks and fails the rejection test, and any fix with validation but other wording also fails its exact message.

deciding_assertions: proxy.spec 'should authenticate': after proxy auth works, goto /protected.html (407 without Proxy-Authorization, else 401 Basic) must give status 401 and body 'no credentials' (no Authorization header sent to the site).
reason: The test is the issue's own case: launch proxy credentials must answer only the proxy 407 and never the site's 401. The narrowest reasonable fix, the one the issue suggests (keep proxy credentials apart from httpCredentials and choose by authChallenge.source in the Chromium network manager), sends no credentials to the 401, so the status is 401 and the body is 'no credentials', while existing proxy-auth tests keep passing.

deciding_assertions: should not hang when git fetch stalls: with a core.sshCommand that runs a node script that sleeps 120 s (a grandchild of git that holds the pipes), the run must end with exitCode 0, print the existing 'timeout of 3000ms exceeded while running "git fetch origin' line, and leave metadata.gitDiff undefined.
reason: The issue offers three fixes ('any of'): reap the process tree on Windows (taskkill) or abandon the promise, skip the fetch when no credentials are found, or fail fast. The test needs the timeout to settle the promise for a non-credential stall on the test platform. A Windows-only taskkill fix, a credential-skip fix, or a fix that only disables the credential prompt still hangs here. Only a fix that abandons the promise on every platform passes. The timeout message already exists in runGit, so it is not the problem.

deciding_assertions: idle-timeout.spec.ts 'closes the browser after the idle timeout and relaunches it on the next call': response text contains 'browser was closed after 500ms of inactivity'; 'cdp endpoint only disconnects on idle...': CDP pages stay open and the response contains 'connection was closed after 500ms of inactivity'.
reason: The issue asks for --timeout-idle <ms>: close the browser after idle and relaunch it on the next call. It does not ask for a notice in the next tool response, and it does not give that text. The narrowest fix (an idle timer that closes the browser, with lazy relaunch) passes the close and relaunch log checks. It fails the exact notice strings and the CDP disconnect-only behaviour, which the issue does not mention.

deciding_assertions: file-paths.spec.ts '--file-paths=absolute': the server starts with the CLI argument '--file-paths=absolute' and expects absolute console, screenshot and filename links.
reason: The issue proposes a config option named like 'pointerPaths: "absolute" | "relative"'. The test passes the CLI flag --file-paths=absolute, a name that the real fix adds and the issue never gives. A fix that adds a pointerPaths option (config, CLI flag --pointer-paths) makes the paths absolute but fails because the server rejects or ignores --file-paths.

deciding_assertions: page-set-content.spec.ts 'should include shadow roots': page.content() stays light-DOM only, and page.content({ includeShadow: true }) returns the HTML with declarative <template shadowrootmode="open"> for open roots and nothing for closed roots.
reason: The issue asks that content() 'or a documented alternative' show shadow content, and names only the earlier proposal serializableShadowRoots: true. The test needs the new option name includeShadow and needs the default content() unchanged. A fix with content({ serializableShadowRoots: true }), or one that changes the default, fails.

deciding_assertions: loader.spec.ts: 'should use react/jsx-runtime when tsconfig does not configure jsx' (runtime 'react'), 'should respect jsxImportSource from tsconfig' (also ESM), 'should respect classic jsx factory from tsconfig', 'should respect react-jsxdev from tsconfig', 'should respect jsx options from tsconfig references and extends', 'should recompile when tsconfig jsx options change'.
reason: The issue asks only to add jsxImportSource (or the transform config) to the transform cache hash, so a cached .tsx transform does not keep an old playwright path. The tests need JSX to compile from the tsconfig jsx options, and need react/jsx-runtime as the default in place of playwright's own runtime. The narrowest fix (add jsxImportSource to calculateHash) fails all seven fail-to-pass tests.

deciding_assertions: 'test modifiers should work': failed2 (test.fail with one string) expects description 'reason'; 'should accept a description only': test.fixme('fixme reason') and test.slow('slow reason') annotations carry the description; 'should check types': test.fixme('reason'), test.fail('reason'), test.slow('reason') must type-check.
reason: The issue asks only for test.skip(description), both at run time and in describe blocks. The tests also need the same one-string form for test.fixme, test.fail and test.slow, at run time and in the TypeScript overloads. A fix that adds test.skip(description) (runtime and a skip(description: string) overload) passes the skip and describe cases. It fails the fixme, fail and slow assertions and the tsc check.

deciding_assertions: proxy.spec.ts 'should authenticate': after proxy auth through launch proxy credentials, goto 'http://non-existent.com/protected.html' (407 without Proxy-Authorization, else 401 Basic) gives status 401 and body 'no credentials'.
reason: The issue states the Chromium case (a site's 401 Basic gets the launch proxy credentials) and expects no credentials for the site's 401. It also proposes the fix: keep proxy credentials apart and check authChallenge.source. The narrowest fix answers only 'Proxy' challenges with the proxy credentials, so the site gets no Authorization header, and it passes both assertions and keeps the first proxy-auth check. Confidence is medium only because the issue names Firefox and WebKit just as 'may need'; the verdict assumes the hidden run uses Chromium.

deciding_assertions: validate input: clientCertificates entry with noCertificate:true plus certPath must throw 'noCertificate is set together with cert, key, passphrase or pfx'; should send/intercept ... when noCertificate is set (fetch, browser, persistentContext): pass noCertificate:true for the visited origin and expect 401 and subjectName 'localhost'; should throw when noCertificate and a real certificate are both set: message 'clientCertificates for origin "https://not-matching.com" mix noCertificate with a real certificate'; pass-to-pass 'should not intercept TLS for origins without a client certificate'
reason: The issue asks to restore the documented pre-1.61 behaviour: a certificate for a non-matching origin makes the proxy intercept and send no certificate. The tests instead need a new option noCertificate and two exact new error messages that the issue never gives. The narrowest reasonable fix (intercept all origins again when clientCertificates is set) fails every fail-to-pass test and also breaks the pass-to-pass test that origins without a certificate are not intercepted.

deciding_assertions: golden/to-have-screenshot/aria-snapshot-file/update-aria-snapshot: with update-snapshots=missing, a missing snapshot gives exitCode 0 and passed 1; with update-snapshots=default it gives exitCode 1; config.spec 'should work with undefined values and base': testInfo.config.updateSnapshots toBe 'default'; config loops include updateSnapshots: 'default'
reason: The issue asks for a new value --update-snapshots=missing-no-failure and keeps the existing 'missing' mode unchanged. The tests instead change 'missing' so it no longer fails and add a new default value named 'default'. The narrowest reasonable fix (add missing-no-failure) fails all nine fail-to-pass tests, because 'missing' still fails and 'default' is not a known value.

deciding_assertions: cli-emulation 'set and clear media features': CLI commands set-color-scheme/clear-color-scheme, set-reduced-motion, set-forced-colors, set-contrast, set-media and their clear-* forms output 'await page.emulateMedia({ X: null });'; cli-help 'prints emulation help after storage': an 'Emulation:' heading right after 'Storage:'; emulation.spec: browser_emulate_media accepts null for all five features; empty arguments give error 'Specify at least one media feature to emulate.'
reason: The issue proposes the browser_emulate_media MCP tool and a --color-scheme CLI flag, with enum values only. The tests need ten new playwright-cli daemon commands and a help section the issue never names, null values to clear features, and an exact error text for empty arguments. A reasonable fix that adds the tool with the listed enum values passes the tool-list test but fails the CLI, help, null and empty-argument tests.

deciding_assertions: All nine tests: reporter name 'failures', CLI flag --reporter-only-failures, reporter option onlyFailures for json/junit/html, env PLAYWRIGHT_FAILURES_OMIT_TAGS; --reporter-only-failures filters json, junit and html reports to failing/flaky tests and keeps blob reports complete, also in merge-reports
reason: The issue offers two options: a new reporter (example name 'only-failures') or a quiet/failuresOnly option on the list reporter. The tests need a reporter named 'failures', a new CLI flag and a per-reporter onlyFailures option, and they check filtering of json, junit and html reports, which the issue does not ask for. A reasonable fix (an 'only-failures' reporter or a list option) fails every test.

deciding_assertions: locator-any-frame 'should treat elements inside hidden iframe as hidden' and locator-frame 'should wait for hidden iframe to become visible': button.click({timeout:1000}) error message must contain 'element is inside a hidden frame, retrying'; also isVisible/isHidden/toBeHidden/waitFor for visibility:hidden iframe, hidden parent, nested iframe and cross-origin iframe
reason: The visibility part follows from the issue: a fix that also checks the computed visibility of each owner frame element passes isVisible, toBeHidden, waitFor and the nested and parent cases. But two fail-to-pass tests also require click to retry with the exact new log line 'element is inside a hidden frame, retrying'. The issue mentions neither click nor any message, so a reasonable fix that reports 'element is not visible' or that does not change click fails these tests.

deciding_assertions: 'should reject invalid signCount': create('example.com', { signCount: -1 }) must reject with message containing 'signCount must be between 0 and 4294967295, got -1' and store no credential
reason: Seeding signCount, returning it from create and get, and the counter increments follow from the issue and the existing counter logic. But one fail-to-pass test needs range validation with an exact message that the issue does not ask for or give. The narrowest reasonable fix (accept signCount and return it, no validation or other wording) fails this test.

deciding_assertions: proxy.spec 'should authenticate': with launch proxy credentials, after a 407-authenticated navigation, goto protected.html (proxy-authorized request gets 401 WWW-Authenticate Basic) must give status 401 and body 'no credentials'
reason: The test checks the issue's own case: launch proxy credentials must not answer the website's 401 challenge. The narrowest reasonable fix (keep proxy credentials apart from httpCredentials and answer only challenges whose authChallenge.source is 'Proxy', as the issue suggests) gives 401 with no Authorization header, for warm and cold proxy-auth cache, and keeps the existing proxy auth tests passing.

deciding_assertions: should not hang when git fetch stalls: core.sshCommand is a node script that hangs as a grandchild of git; expects exitCode 0, output contains 'timeout of 3000ms exceeded while running "git fetch origin', gitDiff undefined
reason: The issue offers three fixes ('any of'): reap the tree on Windows or abandon the promise on timeout, skip the fetch when no credentials are configured, or fail fast on the credential prompt. The test simulates a stall with a hanging ssh command (not a credential prompt) on a non-Windows runner, so only a platform-independent hard timeout that prints the existing timeout message passes; a fix that skips the fetch without credentials, disables the credential prompt (GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0), or uses taskkill on win32 only, fails.

deciding_assertions: idle-timeout.spec.ts: after relaunch the response text contains 'browser was closed after 500ms of inactivity' (once, not on the next call); cdp test expects only a disconnect, pages kept, and 'connection was closed after 500ms of inactivity'; isolated test expects the 'create browser (isolated)' / 'connect to shared browser' log counts
reason: The issue asks for --timeout-idle that closes the browser after idle time and relaunches on the next call; it asks for no notice. The narrowest fix (timer per backend that closes the browser, lazy relaunch) passes the close and relaunch counts but fails the exact notice text in the next response, and the cdp-endpoint behaviour (disconnect only, different notice) is a case the issue does not mention.

deciding_assertions: file-paths.spec.ts '--file-paths=absolute': starts the server with the CLI flag --file-paths=absolute, then expects absolute console log and screenshot links
reason: The issue names a config option 'pointerPaths: "absolute" | "relative"'. The test passes the new CLI flag --file-paths, which the real fix adds and the issue does not give. A fix that adds pointerPaths (config key and a matching --pointer-paths flag) makes the links absolute but the server does not accept --file-paths, so the test fails.

deciding_assertions: page-set-content.spec.ts 'should include shadow roots': page.content() still omits shadow roots; page.content({ includeShadow: true }) returns the HTML with open shadow roots as <template shadowrootmode="open"> and no closed roots
reason: The issue asks that page.content() or a documented alternative shows shadow content, and cites the earlier proposal page.content({ serializableShadowRoots: true }) while it says it does not ask for that exact form. The test needs the new option name includeShadow; a fix with serializableShadowRoots, a new method, or a changed default for content() fails one of the two assertions.

deciding_assertions: loader.spec.ts: JSX with no tsconfig jsx setting must use react/jsx-runtime (runtime 'react'); tsconfig jsxImportSource, classic jsxFactory/jsxFragmentFactory, react-jsxdev, and extends/references must be respected; recompile when tsconfig jsx options change
reason: The issue asks only to add jsxImportSource (or the transform config) to the transform cache hash, so a cached .tsx spec does not import a stale playwright path. All seven fail-to-pass tests check a different feature: JSX compiled with the tsconfig jsx options and the react runtime instead of the Playwright jsx-runtime. The narrowest fix (jsxImportSource in calculateHash) passes none of them.

deciding_assertions: should check types: test.fixme('reason'), test.fail('reason'), test.slow('reason') must type-check; should work: failed2 test.fail('reason') gets description 'reason'; should accept a description only: fixme and slow annotations get the description
reason: The issue asks only for test.skip(description). A fix that adds the skip(description: string) overload and the runtime handling for skip passes the skip cases (in a test and in a describe block) but fails the type check and the annotation checks for fixme, fail and slow, which the issue does not mention. These are sibling modifiers with their own overloads, not the same operation.

deciding_assertions: proxy.spec.ts 'should authenticate': after proxy auth, goto non-existent.com/protected.html returns 401 and the body is 'no credentials' (no Authorization header sent to the site); first part (proxy auth works) unchanged
reason: The issue states the case and suggests the fix: keep proxy credentials apart from httpCredentials and answer only Proxy challenges with them. The narrowest Chromium fix (check event.authChallenge.source, give proxy credentials only to 'Proxy', no site credentials for 'Server') keeps proxy auth working and gives the 401 page with 'no credentials', so it passes. Confidence is medium only because the packet does not say which browser project runs the test; the issue names Chromium and says Firefox/WebKit may need the same check.
